previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and a history of amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He presented with a heart rate of 170, hypoglycemia, and elevated thyroid levels. Management included IV diltiazem for rate control, correction of hypoglycemia and hyperkalemia, and initiation of prednisone and increased methimazole for thyroid storm. He was transitioned to oral diltiazem ER and had stable heart rates by discharge. Peripheral artery disease was diagnosed via ABI testing, and a lidocaine patch was started for leg pain. Hypoglycemia led to temporary discontinuation of Lantus, later restarted at a higher dose. Atorvastatin was held due to myalgias. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home with services, and will follow up with endocrinology, vascular surgery, and nephrology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Thyrotoxicosis of other specified origin without mention of thyrotoxic crisis or storm

Brief Hospital Course:
Primary reason for hospitalization:  ___ year old man PMHx of 
chronic sCHF (40-45%), IDDM, HTN/HL, ESRD on HD ___, 
___, AFib/flutter admitted after a fall at home suspected to be 
related to Afib with RVR.

Active Diagnoses:
# Fall:  Suspected to be secondary to atrial fibrillation with 
rapid ventricular response.  He triggered for this after arrival 
on the floor, with good response to 10mg IV diltiazem.  He was 
given a loading dose of digoxin, and maintained on .125mcg 
daily.He was therapeutic for the first time on Digoxin and he 
was in rate controlled atrial fibrillation for majority of 
admission with HR in 70-90's.   He will need follow-up as an 
outpatient with possible further titration and digoxin level 
monitoring.  He was not anticoagulated given a history of GI 
bleeding.

#Hyperkalemia- the patient was hyperkalemic with no EKG changes 
for the last several days of admission. Given Kayexalate several 
times with stable potassium between ___. Dialysis was not 
lowering potassium and it was thought that potentially Bactrim, 
lisinopril and underlying diabetic nephropathy can be 
contributing to his hyperkalemia. Patient was thought to 
possibly also have some dietary noncompliance with low potassium 
diet.
Please follow as an outpatient and monitor his potassium. Please 
reconsidering changing these medications if hyperkalemia 
persist. he was discharged on low potassium diet.

# HCAP:  Initially had a cough, fever, and focal exam consistent 
with possible pneumonia.  He was treated with 7d course of Vanco 
and Ceftazidime given his risk factors.His cough significantly 
improved and he was asymptomatic and on room air on the day of 
discharge.

Chronic diagnoses:
# ESRD on HD:  Continued HD per renal team.  Transplant surgery 
did not wish to intervene on chronic access this admission.

# Amiodarone induced hyperthyroidism, likely type II:  Followed 
by endocrine as outpatient.  On methimazole and prednisone daily 
dosing, which was continued this admission.Will need TSH 
monitoring as outpatient.

# T2DM:  Home Lantus with sliding scale.

# HTN: Continued home regimen 

# Chronic sCHF:  Continued lisinopril, aspirin.  No beta-blocker 
given cocaine use.  Holding statin given h/o myalgias.  Defer to 
PCP regarding whether to restart statin, per notes, PCP is 
___.

# Chronic lower extremity pain.  Continued lidocaine patch and 
gabapentin

Transitional issues:
#) Digoxin started, will need further titration and monitoring.

#) Needs 24 hour support due to fall risk.

#) Hyperthyroidism - needs continued outpatient follow-up

#) Hyperkalemia- could be medication induced (please see above), 
consider monitoring and appropriate medication titration if 
needed.

being down.  There are new interstitial and focal airspace opacities in both
lungs.  Also noted is a new small right effusion.  A left-sided subclavian
catheter terminates in the right atrium appropriately.  The cardiac silhouette
is enlarged.  The mediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  No
pneumothorax is present.
